research_questions.question: How do charges, expected concessions, denials and credit losses differ in a provider close?
research_questions.scope: Selected US nongovernmental health-care and social-assistance provider roles; synthetic periods and payer purposes stated separately.
research_questions.answer: Record the supported consideration after contract and collectibility assessment, not the charge list alone. Keep subsequent entitlement changes distinct from deterioration in an existing receivable. The synthetic payer and patient balances retain that separation.

research_questions.question: How does a social-assistance award differ from a customer or patient contract?
research_questions.scope: Selected US nongovernmental health-care and social-assistance provider roles; synthetic periods and payer purposes stated separately.
research_questions.answer: For the assumed nonexchange award, a measurable barrier plus return right keeps the unearned advance refundable. data.period: Synthetic 2026 service close, with a separate FY2025 institutional cost-report settlement worksheet; dated official sources accessed 2026-09-19

assumptions: Nongovernmental hospital, with contract criteria and completed service assumed; all amounts are synthetic batch inputs, not rates or actual coverage decisions.

Charges of $100,000 are a billing memorandum, not initial GL revenue. Contractual reductions are $40,000; the remaining $60,000 assigns $50,000 to payer and $10,000 to patient. An expected $5,000 patient price concession gives initial revenue $55,000.
A later documented payer decision reduces entitlement by $3,000, with no patient transfer. Separately, patient credit deterioration creates a supplied $2,000 allowance without changing the price.
An opening $2,000 payer overpayment is repaid through a provider-level offset in the bank deposit; it is not a denial on this batch.

evidence_chain.control: Document contract and estimates separately from claim processing.
4,500,000 claim-payment cents minus 200,000 provider-level offset equals 4,300,000 bank cents.

charity_disclosure.funding_note: No associated charity funding is received in this synthetic case. Any funding in a different case must be reconciled and disclosed separately, not netted against the cost measure.
charity_disclosure.eligibility: Assumed eligible under the stated assistance policy; cost disclosure guidance does not establish eligibility.

assumptions: Independent rendering medical group receives a three-month $90,000 advance under a synthetic Medicaid-plan sub-capitation contract, 100 covered members at $300 per month.

The service promise is an evenly satisfied stand-ready obligation under the assumed accounting scope; one month completed. Insurance-risk transfer, stop-loss, quality incentives and onerous-contract questions are outside the selected example.
Encounter values document utilization and are not additional fee-for-service receivables in this branch; provider is not the state-contracted plan.

Separate nongovernmental residential-care operator provides a daily care service, with no identified asset controlled by the resident under the selected contract. A lease component, if present, requires separate analysis.
Advance covers 30 days at $150 per day; 10 service days completed. A separately refundable $1,000 deposit remains a liability and does not pay for current service. State deposit law not assessed.
Nongovernmental nonprofit, nonexchange award with a measurable per-meal barrier and return right. It is not a customer service contract.
A $10,000 advance supports up to 500 eligible meals at $20 each; the agreement releases each verified unit separately. 300 eligible meals are verified by cutoff.

The only donor purpose restriction is the same meal service and is met as the barrier is satisfied; a consistently applied same-period reporting policy is assumed. A time restriction or different terms would change classification.
Separate incremental FY2025 hospital settlement worksheet starts with a previously recognized $5,000 estimate and balanced opening equity. It is not an assertion of a full hospital balance sheet.

A synthetic MAC notice supports $4,400 under the selected contract; estimate revision reduces revenue by $600 and cash clears the receivable. The notice amount is an input, not calculated from the cost report.
The book-to-cost-center population is $30,000, with $20,000 in center A and $10,000 in center B. Reporting reconciliation alone proves no reimbursement entitlement.

examples.expected: Provider-responsibility adjustment does not create a patient receivable; do not move the $3,000 denial to the patient without a valid basis.
The $2,000 prior overpayment offset settles an existing liability; it does not reduce this batch revenue again.
An expected price concession and subsequent credit deterioration remain separately supported and classified.
Do not add invented fee-for-service revenue for 12 utilization encounters to the earned member-month payment.
A government-owned hospital requires the applicable GASB or federal route, not automatic FASB nonprofit classification.
A nursing-facility cost report cannot use the hospital form merely because both entities furnish care.
Assistance-policy charity is not automatically a collectibility allowance or revenue equal to gross charges.
Refundable security money remains separate from care-service consideration.
A measurable barrier and return right can keep an unearned contribution advance refundable; donor and customer are different roles.
